source.text: וְנֶ֣פֶשׁ כִּֽי־תֶחֱטָ֗א וְשָֽׁמְעָה֙ ק֣וֹל אָלָ֔ה וְה֣וּא עֵ֔ד א֥וֹ רָאָ֖ה א֣וֹ יָדָ֑ע אִם־ל֥וֹא יַגִּ֖יד וְנָשָׂ֥א עֲוֺנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [a] person when it sins and hears [the] voice of [an] oath, and he [is a] witness, or he saw or he knew, if not he tells, then he will bear his iniquity.

en.L: And if anyone sins in that he hears the voice of a curse and he [is] a witness, whether he has seen or known, if he does not tell, then he shall bear his iniquity.
en.B: If someone hears a public call for witnesses made under a curse, and they saw what happened or know about it but do not speak up, they have sinned and will carry their guilt.
en.R: Someone may see or know about a wrong that was done. Then they may hear a call for witnesses, with a curse on anyone who keeps quiet. If they still say nothing, they have sinned. They are guilty and must answer for it.

decisions.choice: the voice of a curse: a public charge to testify, backed by a curse
decisions.reason: The word is the one for an oath that calls down a curse. When a wrong had been done, a curse could be pronounced in public on anyone who knew something and kept silent (Judges 17:2; Proverbs 29:24). Whoever then held back what they knew had sinned. This verse is the first of four cases (verses 1-4) that lead to the confession and offering of verses 5-6. Chapter 4 continues here: the speech that began at 4:2 goes on through verse 13.

decisions.choice: bear his iniquity: carry the guilt of the wrong, and be answerable for it
decisions.reason: The noun means a wrong and also the guilt and punishment that follow from it (Genesis 4:13). To "bear" it is to be held responsible and to remain liable until it is dealt with. The phrase is used of the one who must answer for a sin (verse 17; 7:18; 17:16; 20:17) and also of one who carries the sin of others away (10:17; 16:22). Here the silent witness carries their own guilt; verses 5-6 show how it can be removed.

decisions.choice: anyone: any person, man or woman
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a living person, as in 4:2. The laws of this chapter apply to men and women alike.

decisions.choice: carry their guilt / are guilty and must answer for it
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "bear his iniquity". Balanced says "carry their guilt", and Readable says what that means in plain words. For a person who may be a man or a woman, Balanced and Readable use "they"; Literal keeps "he".

decisions.choice: Someone may see or know ... Then they may hear a call for witnesses
decisions.reason: Readable tells the case in the order the events happen and explains what the "voice of a curse" was.

source.text: א֣וֹ נֶ֗פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּגַּע֮ בְּכָל־דָּבָ֣ר טָמֵא֒ אוֹ֩ בְנִבְלַ֨ת חַיָּ֜ה טְמֵאָ֗ה א֤וֹבְּנִבְלַת֙ בְּהֵמָ֣ה טְמֵאָ֔ה א֕וֹ בְּנִבְלַ֖ת שֶׁ֣רֶץ טָמֵ֑א וְנֶעְלַ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְה֥וּא טָמֵ֖א וְאָשֵֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: Or [a] person who touches any thing unclean, or [the] carcass of [a] wild animal unclean, or [the] carcass of livestock unclean, or [the] carcass of [a] swarming thing unclean, and it is hidden from him, and he [is] unclean, and he is guilty.

en.L: Or if a person touches any unclean thing, whether the carcass of an unclean wild animal, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of an unclean swarming thing, and it is hidden from him, and he [is] unclean, then he is guilty.
en.B: Or someone may touch anything unclean, such as the dead body of an unclean wild animal, unclean livestock or an unclean creature that swarms, without realizing it. They have become unclean and are guilty.
en.R: Or someone may touch something that is unclean, like the dead body of an unclean animal, whether wild or tame, or of a small creature that swarms on the ground. They may not notice it. But they are now unclean and guilty.

decisions.choice: unclean: unfit to come near what is holy
decisions.reason: Unclean is a state, not in itself a moral fault. A person became unclean by touching a dead body, certain animals, or bodily discharges, and could not then come near the sanctuary or eat holy food until made clean again (7:20-21; chapters 11-15). Clean is the ordinary state, holy is what belongs to God, and the two must be kept apart from what is unclean (10:10). Which animals are unclean is set out in chapter 11. The fault in this verse is not the touching itself but staying unclean and letting it reach what is holy.

decisions.choice: it is hidden from him ... he is guilty: he did not know, but is liable once it comes to light
decisions.reason: The person did not notice the contact at the time. The guilt lies in having gone on unclean, perhaps into contact with holy things, without the washing the law requires (11:24-40). Verse 5 says what follows once the person knows.

decisions.choice: a swarming thing: the small creatures that teem on the ground or in water
decisions.reason: The word covers small animals that move in swarms, such as rodents, lizards and insects (11:20-23, 29-31, 41-43).

decisions.choice: dead body; creature that swarms
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "dead body" for "carcass". Readable explains "swarming thing" as a small creature on the ground.

source.text: א֣וֹ כִ֤י יִגַּע֙ בְּטֻמְאַ֣ת אָדָ֔ם לְכֹל֙ טֻמְאָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִטְמָ֖א בָּ֑הּ וְנֶעְלַ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְה֥וּא יָדַ֖ע וְאָשֵֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: Or when he touches [the] uncleanness of [a] human, by any uncleanness of his by which he is unclean, and it is hidden from him, and he knows, and he is guilty.

en.L: Or if he touches human uncleanness, any uncleanness of his by which he becomes unclean, and it is hidden from him, and he comes to know [it], then he is guilty.
en.B: Or someone may come into contact with human uncleanness of any kind that makes a person unclean, and not notice it. Once they learn of it, they are guilty.
en.R: Or someone may touch something from another person that makes them unclean, and not know it. When they find out, they are guilty.

decisions.choice: human uncleanness: what makes a person unclean, as chapters 12-15 describe
decisions.reason: This covers the uncleanness that comes from a human body: from childbirth (12:2-5), skin disease (13:45-46), discharges (15:2-27), and a corpse (Numbers 19:11-16). Touching such a person or thing passes the uncleanness on.

decisions.choice: it is hidden ... and he knows: the guilt is faced when it comes to light
decisions.reason: The two verbs follow one after the other: the person did not know at the time, and later learns of it. The same pattern ends verses 2 and 4.

source.text: א֣וֹ נֶ֡פֶשׁ כִּ֣י תִשָּׁבַע֩ לְבַטֵּ֨א בִשְׂפָתַ֜יִם לְהָרַ֣ע׀א֣וֹ לְהֵיטִ֗יב לְ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְבַטֵּ֧א הָאָדָ֛ם בִּשְׁבֻעָ֖ה וְנֶעְלַ֣ם מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וְהוּא־יָדַ֥ע וְאָשֵׁ֖ם לְאַחַ֥ת מֵאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Or [a] person when it swears, speaking rashly with [the] lips, to do evil or to do good, as to all that [the] human speaks rashly in an oath, and it is hidden from him, and he knows, and he is guilty for one of these.

en.L: Or if a person swears, speaking rashly with [his] lips, to do evil or to do good, in anything that a human may speak rashly in an oath, and it is hidden from him, and he comes to know [it], then he is guilty in one of these.
en.B: Or someone may swear without thinking that they will do something, harmful or good, the kind of oath people make in haste, and then forget it. When they realize it, they are guilty in any of these cases.
en.R: Or someone may make a careless promise and swear to do something, good or bad. People sometimes do this without thinking. If they forget the promise and later remember it, they are guilty.

decisions.choice: speaking rashly with the lips: an oath sworn without thought
decisions.reason: The verb means to blurt out, to speak without thinking. Psalm 106:33 uses it of Moses' rash words. The oath is a promise made before God, which must be kept (Numbers 30:2; Ecclesiastes 5:4-6), even if it was spoken carelessly.

decisions.choice: to do evil or to do good: to do anything at all
decisions.reason: The pair covers every kind of action, harmful or helpful, as in Numbers 24:13. The oath may be a promise to do something or a threat.

decisions.choice: it is hidden ... he comes to know: the oath was forgotten and then remembered
decisions.reason: The person forgot the oath, or did not see what it bound them to, and later realizes it. The words "in one of these" sum up all four cases of verses 1-4.

decisions.choice: If they forget the promise and later remember it
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "it is hidden from him, and he knows" means for an oath.

source.text: וְהָיָ֥ה כִֽי־יֶאְשַׁ֖ם לְאַחַ֣ת מֵאֵ֑לֶּה וְהִ֨תְוַדָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָ֖א עָלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, when he is guilty for one of these, then he will confess [that] which he sinned on it.

en.L: And it shall be, when he is guilty in one of these, that he shall confess that in which he has sinned,
en.B: Whoever is guilty in any of these ways must confess the sin they have committed
en.R: If you are guilty in any of these ways, you must confess what you did wrong.

decisions.choice: confess: say openly what the sin was
decisions.reason: The verb means to acknowledge, to name the wrong aloud. Confession comes before the offering: the guilty person owns what they did. The same is required for the wrongs against a neighbor (Numbers 5:6-7), and on the Day of Atonement the high priest confesses the sins of all Israel (16:21). In 26:40 confession is the way back to God for a whole people.

decisions.choice: when he is guilty in one of these: once the person knows it
decisions.reason: The verse picks up the four cases of verses 1-4. The verb can mean "is guilty" or "realizes their guilt"; either way the confession follows the knowledge of it (verses 3-4).

decisions.choice: you
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the reader as "you" here and in verses 6-13, as chapter 1 does, to keep the instructions short. The Hebrew says "he".

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs into verse 6
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence goes on into verse 6, so Literal ends with a comma and Balanced with no stop.

source.text: וְהֵבִ֣יא אֶת־אֲשָׁמ֣וֹ לַיהוָ֡ה עַ֣ל חַטָּאתוֹ֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר חָטָ֜א נְקֵבָ֨ה מִן־הַצֹּ֥אן כִּשְׂבָּ֛ה אֽוֹ־שְׂעִירַ֥ת עִזִּ֖ים לְחַטָּ֑את וְכִפֶּ֥ר עָלָ֛יו הַכֹּהֵ֖ן מֵחַטָּאתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will bring his guilt to Yahweh for his sin which he sinned, [a] female from the flock, [a] ewe lamb or [a] female goat of goats, for [a] sin offering, and will make atonement for him the priest from his sin.

en.L: and he shall bring his guilt [payment] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for his sin that he has sinned, a female from the flock, a ewe lamb or a female goat, for a sin offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin.
en.B: and bring to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} what is owed for the sin: a female animal from the flock, a lamb or a goat, as a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for them for their sin.
en.R: To make up for your sin, bring a female lamb or a female goat to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for you for your sin.

decisions.choice: his guilt: what the guilty person must pay to set the wrong right
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the guilt offering of verses 15-26, but here the animal is a sin offering, as the verse says. So the word has its wider sense: the penalty or payment owed because of guilt. The same wider sense is used of the Philistines' gold sent back with the ark (1 Samuel 6:3-4). See the note at verse 15.

decisions.choice: a female from the flock: the offering of an ordinary Israelite
decisions.reason: A female lamb or goat is what an ordinary member of the people brings as a sin offering (4:28, 32). The rite is the one set out in 4:27-35.

decisions.choice: make atonement for him for his sin: as in 1:4 and 4:20
decisions.reason: The priest's rite removes the sin that stands between the person and God.

decisions.choice: his guilt [payment]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "payment" to show that the word here is not the name of an offering. Balanced says "what is owed", and Readable "to make up for".

source.text: וְאִם־לֹ֨א תַגִּ֣יעיָדוֹ֮ דֵּ֣י שֶׂה֒ וְהֵבִ֨יא אֶת־אֲשָׁמ֜וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֗א שְׁתֵּ֥י תֹרִ֛ים אֽוֹ־שְׁנֵ֥י בְנֵֽי־יוֹנָ֖ה לַֽיהוָ֑ה אֶחָ֥ד לְחַטָּ֖את וְאֶחָ֥ד לְעֹלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And if not his hand reaches [the] sufficiency of [a] sheep, then he will bring his guilt which he sinned, two turtledoves or two sons of [a] dove, to Yahweh, one for [a] sin offering and one for [a] burnt offering.

en.L: And if his hand cannot reach enough for a lamb, then he shall bring [as] his guilt [payment] for what he has sinned two turtledoves or two young pigeons to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
en.B: If a lamb is more than they can afford, they may bring {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} two turtledoves or two young pigeons to pay for their sin. One of them is for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering.
en.R: If you do not have enough money for a lamb, bring two doves or two young pigeons to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for your sin. One will be for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering.

decisions.choice: his hand cannot reach enough: he cannot afford it
decisions.reason: "The hand reaches" means to have the means. The law allows a smaller offering for the poor, in steps: birds here, and flour in verse 11. The same provision is made in 12:8 and 14:21-22. No one is shut out from atonement because of poverty; Mary and Joseph brought the birds after Jesus' birth (Luke 2:24).

decisions.choice: two birds: one sin offering and one burnt offering
alternatives: one bird offered in place of the fat
decisions.reason: A bird is too small to give fat for the altar as a lamb does (4:31), so a second bird is burned whole as a burnt offering, as in 1:14-17. The sin offering is offered first (verse 8).

decisions.choice: his guilt: what is owed for the sin, as in verse 6
decisions.reason: Here too the word names the payment owed, not the guilt offering of verse 15.

decisions.choice: doves
decisions.reason: Readable says "doves" for turtledoves, as in 1:14.

source.text: וְהֵבִ֤יא אֹתָם֙ אֶל־הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהִקְרִ֛יב אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לַחַטָּ֖את רִאשׁוֹנָ֑ה וּמָלַ֧ק אֶת־רֹאשׁ֛וֹ מִמּ֥וּל עָרְפּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֥א יַבְדִּֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will bring them to the priest, and he will bring near [the one] which [is] for the sin offering first, and he will nip off its head from in front of its neck, and not he will divide [it].

en.L: And he shall bring them to the priest, and he shall bring near first the one that [is] for the sin offering, and he shall nip off its head from the front of its neck, but he shall not sever [it].
en.B: The priest receives them and first presents the bird for the sin offering. He breaks its neck at the front but does not pull the head off.
en.R: Give them to the priest. He will offer the bird for the sin offering first. He will break its neck but not pull off its head.

decisions.choice: nip off its head ... not sever it: the neck is broken but the head stays attached
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 1:15 for the bird burnt offering, where the head is removed. Here the priest breaks or cuts the neck at the front without taking the head right off, perhaps so that the blood can be drained for the rite of verse 9.

decisions.choice: the sin offering first: dealing with sin comes before the gift
decisions.reason: The sin offering comes before the burnt offering, as in the ordination rites (8:14-21) and the eighth-day offerings (9:8-14).

decisions.choice: breaks / break its neck
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "nip off", as in 1:15. Balanced and Readable describe what is done, since the head is not taken off.

source.text: וְהִזָּ֞ה מִדַּ֤ם הַחַטָּאת֙ עַל־קִ֣יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְהַנִּשְׁאָ֣ר בַּדָּ֔ם יִמָּצֵ֖ה אֶל־יְס֣וֹד הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ חַטָּ֖את הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will sprinkle some of [the] blood of the sin offering on [the] wall of the altar, and the remainder of the blood will be drained out at [the] base of the altar; [a] sin offering it [is].

en.L: And he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar; it [is] a sin offering.
en.B: Some of its blood he is to sprinkle on the side of the altar, and what is left is to be pressed out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
en.R: He will sprinkle some of its blood on the side of the altar. Then he will drain the rest of the blood out at the bottom of the altar. It is a sin offering.

decisions.choice: sprinkle ... drain out at the base: the blood rite for a bird
decisions.reason: With a bird there is too little blood to put on the horns of the altar (4:30). Some is sprinkled on the altar's side and the rest pressed out at its base, where the blood of the larger sin offerings is poured out (4:7, 30).

decisions.choice: it is a sin offering: the rite counts as the full offering
decisions.reason: The closing words state that this smaller rite is a true sin offering and does what the lamb or goat does (verse 6).

source.text: וְאֶת־הַשֵּׁנִ֛י יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה עֹלָ֖ה כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וְכִפֶּ֨ר עָלָ֧יו הַכֹּהֵ֛ן מֵחַטָּאת֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־חָטָ֖א וְנִסְלַ֥ח לֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the second he will make [a] burnt offering according to the ordinance, and will make atonement for him the priest from his sin which he sinned, and it will be forgiven to him.

en.L: And the second he shall make a burnt offering according to the ordinance; and the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin that he has sinned, and it will be forgiven him.
en.B: He is to offer the second bird as a burnt offering in the prescribed way. Through this the priest makes atonement for them for their sin, and they will be forgiven.
en.R: He will offer the second bird as a burnt offering in the way the law requires. In this way the priest will make atonement for you for your sin, and you will be forgiven.

decisions.choice: according to the ordinance: the rite for a bird burnt offering in 1:14-17
decisions.reason: The word means a ruling or the set way of doing something. The burnt offering of a bird is to be done as already laid down.

decisions.choice: it will be forgiven him: as in 4:20
decisions.reason: God forgives; the passive leaves him unnamed, as the verb is always used of God's forgiving. The poor person's two birds bring the same forgiveness as a lamb.

decisions.choice: they will be forgiven
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "they" for the worshiper, who may be a man or a woman (see 4:20).

source.text: וְאִם־לֹא֩ תַשִּׂ֨יג יָד֜וֹ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י תֹרִ֗ים אוֹ֮ לִשְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵי־יוֹנָה֒ וְהֵבִ֨יא אֶת־קָרְבָּנ֜וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֗א עֲשִׂירִ֧ת הָאֵפָ֛ה סֹ֖לֶת לְחַטָּ֑את לֹא־יָשִׂ֨ים עָלֶ֜יהָ שֶׁ֗מֶן וְלֹא־יִתֵּ֤ן עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ לְבֹנָ֔ה כִּ֥י חַטָּ֖את הִֽיא׃

records.literal_gloss: And if not his hand reaches to two turtledoves or to two sons of [a] dove, then he will bring his offering, [he] who sinned, [a] tenth of the ephah of fine flour for [a] sin offering; not he will put on it oil, and not he will put on it frankincense, for [a] sin offering it [is].

en.L: And if his hand cannot reach two turtledoves or two young pigeons, then he who has sinned shall bring as his offering a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering; he shall not put oil on it, nor shall he put frankincense on it, for it [is] a sin offering.
en.B: If even two turtledoves or two young pigeons are beyond their means, the one who sinned is to bring {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour as a sin offering. No oil or frankincense is to be put on it, since it is a sin offering.
en.R: If you cannot pay for two doves or two young pigeons, bring {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour as a sin offering. Do not put any oil or frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering, not a gift.

decisions.choice: a tenth of an ephah: about two quarts or two liters of flour
decisions.reason: The ephah was a dry measure of roughly 20 to 22 liters (about three-fifths of a bushel), so a tenth was about two liters. It is the same amount as the omer of manna, one person's food for a day (Exodus 16:16, 36). It is also the daily grain offering of the priest (6:13) and the flour that goes with a lamb (Numbers 28:5). The size of the ephah is known only approximately.

decisions.choice: no oil or frankincense: this is a sin offering, not a grain offering
alternatives: the offering is plain because of the sin
decisions.reason: A grain offering has oil and frankincense put on it (2:1); this flour has neither. It is offered for sin, and is not a gift of joy or a pleasing aroma. Even without blood it makes atonement for the very poor (verse 13).

decisions.choice: his hand cannot reach: as in verse 7
decisions.reason: This is the last step down for the poorest.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure, with the original unit as the setting alternative. Literal keeps "a tenth of an ephah".

decisions.choice: not a gift
decisions.reason: Readable adds "not a gift" to explain why the oil and frankincense of the grain offering are left off.

source.text: וֶהֱבִיאָהּ֮ אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן֒ וְקָמַ֣ץ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן׀מִ֠מֶּנָּה מְל֨וֹא קֻמְצ֜וֹ אֶת־אַזְכָּרָתָה֙ וְהִקְטִ֣יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה עַ֖ל אִשֵּׁ֣י יְהוָ֑ה חַטָּ֖את הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will bring it to the priest, and will take a handful the priest from it, [the] fullness of his handful, its memorial portion, and will make [it] smoke on the altar on [the] fire offerings of Yahweh; [a] sin offering it [is].

en.L: And he shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take a handful from it, his handful, its memorial portion, and make [it] smoke on the altar on the offerings by fire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; it [is] a sin offering.
en.B: The flour is brought to the priest. He takes a full handful from it as its memorial portion and turns it into smoke on the altar, with the food offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is a sin offering.
en.R: Give it to the priest. He will take a handful of it as the part that is a reminder, and burn it on the altar along with the food offerings burned for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is a sin offering.

decisions.choice: a handful as its memorial portion: as with the grain offering in 2:2
decisions.reason: The priest takes a full handful and burns it as the portion that stands for the whole before God (see 2:2).

decisions.choice: on the offerings by fire of the LORD: on what is already burning on the altar
decisions.reason: The handful is laid on the offerings already on the altar fire (compare 3:5). On the term see 1:9.

source.text: וְכִפֶּר֩ עָלָ֨יו הַכֹּהֵ֜ן עַל־חַטָּאת֧וֹ אֲשֶׁר־חָטָ֛א מֵֽאַחַ֥ת מֵאֵ֖לֶּה וְנִסְלַ֣ח ל֑וֹ וְהָיְתָ֥ה לַכֹּהֵ֖ן כַּמִּנְחָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And will make atonement for him the priest for his sin which he sinned from one of these, and it will be forgiven to him; and it will be for the priest like the grain offering.

en.L: And the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin that he has sinned in any one of these, and it will be forgiven him; and [the rest] shall be the priest's, like the grain offering.'"
en.B: The priest is to make atonement for them for the sin they committed in any one of these cases; then they will be forgiven. The rest of the flour belongs to the priest, as with the grain offering.'"
en.R: The priest will make atonement for you for whichever of these sins you did. Then you will be forgiven. The rest of the flour belongs to the priest, as with the grain offering.'"

decisions.choice: it will be forgiven him: as in verse 10 and 4:20
decisions.reason: The flour offering of the poorest brings the same forgiveness as the lamb of verse 6.

decisions.choice: it will be the priest's like the grain offering: the priest eats the rest
decisions.reason: As with the grain offering (2:3, 10; 6:9-11), what is left after the handful is burned belongs to the priests (compare 6:19, 22).

decisions.choice: the end of the speech that began at 4:2
decisions.reason: The words the LORD gave Moses in 4:1 end here. A new speech begins after the formula in verse 14.

decisions.choice: [the rest] / The rest of the flour
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "it will be the priest's". What the priest receives is what remains after the handful has been burned, so the levels supply "the rest" (bracketed at Literal).

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: a new speech: the guilt offering
decisions.reason: The formula opens the instructions for the guilt offering, in two speeches (verses 15-19 and 20-26). Unlike 4:2, these speeches do not tell Moses to pass them on to the people, but the cases are about anyone in Israel.

source.text: נֶ֚פֶשׁ כִּֽי־תִמְעֹ֣ל מַ֔עַל וְחָֽטְאָה֙ בִּשְׁגָגָ֔ה מִקָּדְשֵׁ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וְהֵבִיא֩ אֶת־אֲשָׁמ֨וֹ לַֽיהוָ֜ה אַ֧יִל תָּמִ֣ים מִן־הַצֹּ֗אן בְּעֶרְכְּךָ֛ כֶּֽסֶף־שְׁקָלִ֥ים בְּשֶֽׁקֶל־הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לְאָשָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] person when it acts unfaithfully [an] unfaithfulness and sins in error from [the] holy things of Yahweh, then he will bring his guilt to Yahweh, [a] ram unblemished from the flock, by your valuation [in] silver of shekels by [the] shekel of the holy place, for [a] guilt offering.

en.L: "When a person acts unfaithfully and sins in error against the holy things of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, then he shall bring his guilt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a ram, unblemished, from the flock, by your valuation in silver shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary, for a guilt offering.
en.B: "If anyone sins without intending to and wrongs {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the matter of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy things, they must bring a ram from the flock with no defect to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as their guilt offering. Its value is set in shekels of silver by the sanctuary shekel. It is a guilt offering.
en.R: "Someone may do wrong without meaning to by misusing something holy that belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That is being unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That person must bring a ram from the flock as a guilt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It must have nothing wrong with it. Its value must be set in silver shekels, using the official shekel used at the holy tent.

decisions.choice: a guilt offering: an offering of reparation for what is owed
decisions.reason: The word means guilt, and also the payment that guilt makes due. This offering is for wrongs that have cost someone something: God's holy things misused (verses 15-16), or a neighbor's property taken by fraud (verses 21-24). Unlike the sin offering, it comes with repayment of the loss plus a fifth, and the animal itself is valued in silver. So the offering is a payment of damages to God as well as a sacrifice. The Philistines send back gold with the ark under the same name (1 Samuel 6:3-4), and Isaiah 53:10 says the servant's life is made this offering. It is brought also at the cleansing of a person with skin disease (14:12) and of a Nazirite (Numbers 6:12).

decisions.choice: acts unfaithfully against the holy things: wrongs God by taking or misusing what is his
alternatives: sins in the matter of sacred things
decisions.reason: The verb and its noun describe a breach of trust, the betrayal of a relationship: Achan takes what was devoted to God (Joshua 7:1), and a wife is unfaithful to her husband (Numbers 5:12). "The holy things of the LORD" are what belongs to him: offerings, the priests' portions, tithes and firstborn, which an Israelite might keep back or eat by mistake (22:14-16). The sin is "in error", unintentional (4:2).

decisions.choice: by your valuation in silver shekels, by the sanctuary shekel: the ram is valued in silver at the sanctuary standard
alternatives: a ram worth at least two shekels
a ram or its value in silver
decisions.reason: The shekel was a weight, about 11.5 grams or two-fifths of an ounce of silver; coins were not yet in use (Genesis 23:16). Weights varied, so payments to the sanctuary used the official standard of twenty gerahs (27:25; Exodus 30:13). The phrase "by your valuation" is fixed in these laws (27:2-3). It may mean that the ram must be worth a set amount, at least two shekels since "shekels" is plural, or that its value could be paid in silver instead. The text does not settle which.

decisions.choice: the official shekel used at the holy tent
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the sanctuary shekel was. Literal says "the shekel of the sanctuary" and Balanced "the sanctuary shekel".

decisions.choice: wrongs the LORD / being unfaithful
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb with its noun, "acts unfaithfully". Balanced says "wrongs the LORD in the matter of his holy things", naming whom the wrong is against, as verse 21 does. Readable first says what was done, then names it.

source.text: וְאֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר֩ חָטָ֨א מִן־הַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ יְשַׁלֵּ֗ם וְאֶת־חֲמִֽישִׁתוֹ֙ יוֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֔יו וְנָתַ֥ן אֹת֖וֹ לַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְהַכֹּהֵ֗ן יְכַפֵּ֥ר עָלָ֛יו בְּאֵ֥יל הָאָשָׁ֖ם וְנִסְלַ֥ח לֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And [that] which he sinned from the holy thing he will repay, and its fifth he will add to it, and he will give it to the priest; and the priest will make atonement for him with [the] ram of the guilt offering, and it will be forgiven to him.

en.L: And that in which he sinned against the holy thing he shall repay, and he shall add its fifth to it and give it to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and it will be forgiven him.
en.B: They must also pay back in full what they wrongly kept from the holy things, with a fifth of its value added, and give it to the priest. With the ram of the guilt offering the priest will make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
en.R: They must also pay back what they took from the holy things. They must add one fifth more and give it all to the priest. Then the priest will make atonement for them with the ram, and they will be forgiven.

decisions.choice: repay and add a fifth: restore the loss and twenty percent more
decisions.reason: The verb means to make whole, to pay what is owed. The loss is made good first, and then a fifth of its value is added on top. The same is required for wrongs against a neighbor (verse 24; Numbers 5:7), for holy food eaten by mistake (22:14) and for redeeming what was vowed (27:13, 31). The fifth goes beyond simple restoring: it costs something to have taken what was not one's own.

decisions.choice: give it to the priest ... the ram of the guilt offering: payment and offering both
decisions.reason: The repayment goes to the priest, who acts for the sanctuary, and the ram is offered as well. Atonement comes through the ram; the repayment is required too.

decisions.choice: what they wrongly kept from the holy things
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "that which he sinned from the holy thing". Balanced says what such a sin usually was: keeping back what belonged to the sanctuary. Readable says "took".

source.text: וְאִם־נֶ֨פֶשׁ֙ כִּ֣י תֶֽחֱטָ֔א וְעָֽשְׂתָ֗ה אַחַת֙ מִכָּל־מִצְוֺ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֣א תֵעָשֶׂ֑ינָה וְלֹֽא־יָדַ֥ע וְאָשֵׁ֖ם וְנָשָׂ֥א עֲוֺנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And if [a] person when it sins and does one of all [the] commandments of Yahweh which not should be done, and not he knew, and he is guilty and will bear his iniquity,

en.L: And if a person sins and does any one of all the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that should not be done, and he did not know [it], yet he is guilty and shall bear his iniquity,
en.B: Suppose someone sins by breaking one of the commands of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, doing what must not be done, and is unaware of it. They are guilty all the same and will carry their guilt,
en.R: Someone may break one of the commands of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} without knowing it. They are still guilty and must answer for it.

decisions.choice: does one of the commandments that should not be done: breaks a prohibition
alternatives: a case where the wrong to the holy things is only suspected
decisions.reason: The wording repeats 4:2, 13, 22, 27. Here the sin is done without knowing, and the person may not be sure what they did. The guilt offering is required; the text does not say what holy thing is involved.

decisions.choice: bear his iniquity: be held answerable, as in verse 1
decisions.reason: Not knowing does not remove the guilt.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs into verse 18
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence goes on into verse 18, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma. Readable makes two sentences.

source.text: וְ֠הֵבִיא אַ֣יִל תָּמִ֧ים מִן־הַצֹּ֛אן בְּעֶרְכְּךָ֥ לְאָשָׁ֖ם אֶל־הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְכִפֶּר֩ עָלָ֨יו הַכֹּהֵ֜ן עַ֣ל שִׁגְגָת֧וֹ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁגָ֛ג וְה֥וּא לֹֽא־יָדַ֖ע וְנִסְלַ֥ח לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: then he will bring [a] ram unblemished from the flock by your valuation for [a] guilt offering to the priest, and will make atonement for him the priest for his error which he erred, and he not knew, and it will be forgiven to him.

en.L: then he shall bring a ram, unblemished, from the flock, by your valuation, for a guilt offering to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him for his error that he committed in error, and he did not know [it], and it will be forgiven him.
en.B: and must bring a ram without defect from the flock, of the set value, to the priest as a guilt offering. So the priest will make atonement for them for the error they did not know they had made, and they will be forgiven.
en.R: They must bring a ram from the flock to the priest as a guilt offering. It must have nothing wrong with it and be worth the set price. The priest will make atonement for them for the wrong they did without knowing it. Then they will be forgiven.

decisions.choice: by your valuation: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The ram is valued in silver by the sanctuary standard, as in verse 15.

decisions.choice: his error that he committed in error: the noun and verb of unintentional sin
decisions.reason: The noun and verb are the ones translated "in error" in 4:2. Repeating them stresses that the sin was not deliberate. Deliberate sin is dealt with differently (Numbers 15:27-31).

source.text: אָשָׁ֖ם ה֑וּא אָשֹׁ֥ם אָשַׁ֖ם לַיהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: [A] guilt offering it [is]; he was surely guilty to Yahweh.

en.L: It [is] a guilt offering; he has surely become guilty before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: It is a guilt offering. They have certainly become guilty before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: It is a guilt offering, because they really are guilty before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: he has surely become guilty before the LORD
alternatives: he must make full reparation to the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. It can mean "he is certainly guilty before the LORD", which explains why an offering is needed even when the sin was unknown, or "he must surely pay what he owes to the LORD", which links it with the guilt offering just named.

decisions.choice: because
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two statements with "because" to show how the second explains the first. Literal and Balanced keep two clauses.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: verse numbers follow the Hebrew text: 5:20-26 here are 6:1-7 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text chapter 5 has 26 verses. Many Bibles end chapter 5 at verse 19 and number Hebrew 5:20-26 as 6:1-7, so that Hebrew 6:1-23 become 6:8-30. This translation follows the Hebrew numbers, and cites Leviticus by them.

decisions.choice: a second speech on the guilt offering: wrongs against a neighbor
decisions.reason: Verses 15-19 dealt with wrongs against holy things. This speech deals with wrongs against another person, which are also counted as unfaithfulness to the LORD (verse 21).

source.text: נֶ֚פֶשׁ כִּ֣י תֶחֱטָ֔א וּמָעֲלָ֥ה מַ֖עַל בַּיהוָ֑ה וְכִחֵ֨שׁ בַּעֲמִית֜וֹ בְּפִקָּד֗וֹן אֽוֹ־בִתְשׂ֤וּמֶת יָד֙ א֣וֹ בְגָזֵ֔ל א֖וֹ עָשַׁ֥ק אֶת־עֲמִיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] person when it sins and acts unfaithfully [an] unfaithfulness against Yahweh, and deceives his fellow in [a] deposit or in [a] placing of [the] hand or in robbery, or he has oppressed his fellow,

en.L: "When a person sins and acts unfaithfully against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and deceives his neighbor about a deposit, or a pledge, or robbery, or has extorted from his neighbor,
en.B: "Suppose someone sins and betrays {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by deceiving a neighbor: denying that they hold goods the neighbor gave them to keep or as security, or taking the neighbor's goods by robbery, or extorting from them,
en.R: "Someone may sin against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by doing wrong to another person. They may lie about something a neighbor left with them to keep safe or gave them as a promise of payment. They may steal from a neighbor or cheat them.

decisions.choice: acts unfaithfully against the LORD: a wrong to a neighbor is also a wrong to God
decisions.reason: The same words were used in verse 15 for misusing holy things. Here the wrong is done to another person, but it is counted as unfaithfulness to the LORD, because the false oath of verse 22 calls on his name and his law protects the neighbor (19:11-13). So the guilty person repays the neighbor and brings a guilt offering to God (verses 24-25).

decisions.choice: deceives his neighbor about a deposit or a pledge: denies holding what was entrusted
decisions.reason: The verb means to deny falsely or deceive. A deposit is goods left with someone for safekeeping (Exodus 22:7-13). The next phrase, literally "a placing of the hand", occurs only here; it most likely means something handed over as security for a loan or debt, but it may mean a business agreement made by striking hands. The word for neighbor means a fellow member of the people, a companion.

decisions.choice: robbery ... extorted: taking by force or by pressure
decisions.reason: Robbery is seizing what belongs to another openly (19:13). The verb "extort" means to oppress, to take what is owed by abusing power, such as holding back a worker's wages (19:13; Deuteronomy 24:14).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs into verse 22
decisions.reason: The list of wrongs goes on into verse 22, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma. Readable breaks it into short sentences.

decisions.choice: a neighbor
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "his fellow". "Neighbor" is already inclusive, so no gender setting is needed; Balanced and Readable use "they" for the guilty person.

source.text: אֽוֹ־מָצָ֧א אֲבֵדָ֛ה וְכִ֥חֶשׁ בָּ֖הּ וְנִשְׁבַּ֣ע עַל־שָׁ֑קֶר עַל־אַחַ֗ת מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם לַחֲטֹ֥א בָהֵֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: or he has found [a] lost thing and deceived about it and sworn on falsehood, about one of all that [the] human does, to sin by them,

en.L: or has found something lost and deceived about it, and has sworn falsely, in any one of all the things that a human may do to sin by them,
en.B: or keeping lost property they found and denying it, or taking a false oath about any of the wrongs people commit,
en.R: They may find something that someone lost and say they do not have it. Or they may swear that something is true when it is not. People do these kinds of wrong things.

decisions.choice: found something lost and deceived about it: keeping a neighbor's lost property
decisions.reason: The law requires that what is found be returned to its owner (Deuteronomy 22:1-3; Exodus 23:4). Here the finder denies having it.

decisions.choice: sworn falsely: lying under oath
decisions.reason: Such disputes were settled by an oath before God (Exodus 22:8-11). To swear falsely is to use God's name to support a lie, which 19:12 forbids. The false oath may go with any of the wrongs of verses 21-22.

decisions.choice: People do these kinds of wrong things.
decisions.reason: Readable puts the summing-up phrase "in any of all that a human may do to sin" as a short sentence of its own.

source.text: וְהָיָה֮ כִּֽי־יֶחֱטָ֣א וְאָשֵׁם֒ וְהֵשִׁ֨יב אֶת־הַגְּזֵלָ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר גָּזָ֗ל א֤וֹ אֶת־הָעֹ֨שֶׁק֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׁ֔ק א֚וֹ אֶת־הַפִּקָּד֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָפְקַ֖ד אִתּ֑וֹ א֥וֹ אֶת־הָאֲבֵדָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָצָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: and it will be, when he sins and is guilty, then he will return the robbery which he robbed, or the extortion which he extorted, or the deposit which was entrusted with him, or the lost thing which he found,

en.L: then it shall be, when he has sinned and is guilty, that he shall return what he took by robbery, or what he got by extortion, or the deposit that was entrusted to him, or the lost thing that he found,
en.B: then, being guilty of such a sin, they must hand back the goods they seized by robbery or extortion, the deposit placed with them, or the lost item they found,
en.R: If someone does any of these things, they are guilty. They must give back what they stole or took by cheating. They must give back what was left with them or the lost thing they found.

decisions.choice: when he sins and is guilty: once the wrong is admitted
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the verb may mean "is guilty" or "realizes his guilt". These wrongs are deliberate, but the law gives the way back when the guilty person owns the wrong, which Numbers 5:6-7 says includes confession.

decisions.choice: return: give back the very thing taken
decisions.reason: Each wrong of verses 21-22 is named again, and each is to be undone.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs into verse 24
decisions.reason: The list goes on into verse 24, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma.

source.text: א֠וֹ מִכֹּ֞ל אֲשֶׁר־יִשָּׁבַ֣ע עָלָיו֮ לַשֶּׁקֶר֒ וְשִׁלַּ֤ם אֹתוֹ֙ בְּרֹאשׁ֔וֹ וַחֲמִשִׁתָ֖יו יֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֑יו לַאֲשֶׁ֨ר ה֥וּא ל֛וֹ יִתְּנֶ֖נּוּ בְּי֥וֹם אַשְׁמָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: or anything about which he swore on falsehood; and he will repay it in its head, and its fifths he will add to it; to [the one] whom it [is] his he will give it on [the] day of his guilt.

en.L: or anything at all about which he swore falsely; he shall repay it in full, and he shall add its fifth to it; he shall give it to the one to whom it belongs on the day of his guilt [offering].
en.B: or anything at all that was the subject of their false oath. They must pay it back in full and a fifth more besides, and the owner is to receive it on the day of their guilt offering.
en.R: Or they must give back whatever they lied about under oath. They must pay back all of it, and add one fifth more. They must give it to the owner on the day they bring their guilt offering.

decisions.choice: repay it in its head: repay the full original amount
decisions.reason: "Its head" means the principal, the whole of what was taken (Numbers 5:7). To this a fifth is added, as in verse 16.

decisions.choice: to the one to whom it belongs: the owner is repaid first
decisions.reason: The repayment goes to the neighbor who was wronged, not to the sanctuary. Only if the owner and his next of kin are dead does it go to the priest (Numbers 5:8).

decisions.choice: on the day of his guilt: the day he is found guilty or brings his guilt offering
alternatives: the day he is found guilty
decisions.reason: The word may mean the day the guilt is established or admitted, or the day of the guilt offering. Either way, the neighbor is repaid before the offering is made, as Matthew 5:23-24 also teaches.

decisions.choice: the day of their guilt offering / the day they bring their guilt offering
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the phrase as the day of the offering, which verse 25 then describes. Literal keeps "the day of his guilt" with "offering" in brackets.

source.text: וְאֶת־אֲשָׁמ֥וֹ יָבִ֖יא לַיהוָ֑ה אַ֣יִל תָּמִ֧ים מִן־הַצֹּ֛אן בְּעֶרְכְּךָ֥ לְאָשָׁ֖ם אֶל־הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And his guilt offering he will bring to Yahweh, [a] ram unblemished from the flock, by your valuation, for [a] guilt offering, to the priest.

en.L: And he shall bring his guilt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a ram, unblemished, from the flock, by your valuation, for a guilt offering, to the priest.
en.B: They must bring to the priest their guilt offering for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: a ram without defect from the flock, of the set value.
en.R: They must bring a ram to the priest as a guilt offering for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It must come from the flock, have nothing wrong with it, and be worth the set price.

decisions.choice: a ram by your valuation: the same offering as for the holy things
decisions.reason: The offering is the same as in verses 15 and 18: wrongs against a neighbor need the same atonement as wrongs against holy things. See the note at verse 15.

source.text: וְכִפֶּ֨ר עָלָ֧יו הַכֹּהֵ֛ן לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה וְנִסְלַ֣ח ל֑וֹ עַל־אַחַ֛ת מִכֹּ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה לְאַשְׁמָ֥ה בָֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And will make atonement for him the priest before Yahweh, and it will be forgiven to him, for one of all that he does to [be] guilty by it.

en.L: And the priest shall make atonement for him before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and it will be forgiven him, for any one of all the things that he may do so as to become guilty by it."
en.B: Before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the priest will make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven for any one of the wrongs that brought them guilt."
en.R: The priest will make atonement for them in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then they will be forgiven for any of these wrongs that made them guilty."

decisions.choice: make atonement ... forgiven: as in 1:4 and 4:20
decisions.reason: Even deliberate wrongs against a neighbor can be forgiven when the loss is repaid and the offering made. The speech ends here; chapter 6 opens a new one.

decisions.choice: for any one of all that he may do: every case listed in verses 21-22
decisions.reason: The closing words cover the whole list of wrongs, as "one of these" did in verse 13.
